newsitem.title: KENYA: IMF praises Kenyan efforts to get economy on track.
newsitem.headline: IMF praises Kenyan efforts to get economy on track.

text.p: Kenya is on course to receive a further $37 million in International Monetary Fund assistance after a review of structural reform programmes showed the country had made satisfactory progress in major policy areas.
But the IMF warned on Sunday that progress was still slow -- particularly in privatisation and public enterprise reform -- and urged greater effort in these areas.

In a statement following a mid-term review of Kenya's economy, IMF senior adviser Hiroyuki Hino said he would be recommending the completion of a review which would free up the second tranche of a $74 million enhanced structural adjustment facility.
The three-year facility totals $220 million of which $74 million was for 1996.
Hino said fiscal and monetary policy had been executed broadly in line with recommendations.

"The external balance of payments remained strong and international reserves increased," he said. "Inflation was higher than expected due to the drought, but underlying inflation remained broadly under control.
Hino said, however, that real growth for last year was estimated at 4.6 percent -- below the five percent target.

He said also there were renewed instances of "a lack of discipline" in public finances, particularly an irregular purchases in the ministry of health and the awarding of contracts to independent power producers.
The government has pledged to tighten up internal purchase processes and had also commissioned an independent review of the tender process used in the power contracts.
Hino said the IMF would now review its arrangement with Kenya and, if the reforms were approved, the $37 million would be available in June.
Kenya has asked the World Bank to organise a consultative group meeting in July to discuss how to use the funds.
